lesson: This allowed Qg5, which attacks two things at once: your pawn on g2 and your knight on e5. You can't save both. Look for squares where one enemy piece could hit two of yours.
You hung your pawn on g2 -- it was left unprotected, and they can take it with Qxg2. Blunder check: is the square I'm moving to attacked? Did my move leave anything undefended?
You hung your pawn on e4 -- it was left unprotected, and they can take it with Qxe4+. Blunder check: is the square I'm moving to attacked? Did my move leave anything undefended?
